scan_linter_check.description:
Flags string literals that are credentials: - assigned to a variable, property or object key whose name ends in a credential word (password, passwd, pwd, passphrase, secret, token, apiKey/api_key, accessKey, privateKey, secretKey, credential), for example dbPassword or clientSecret. Names like passwordPolicy or tokenUrl are not credentials. - passed as the password to setBasicAuth(), setPassword() or setMIDServerPassword(), as the Authorization header value (Basic or Bearer) to setRequestHeader(), or as the value of a header or REST parameter whose name is a credential name - in a known credential format anywhere: AWS access key IDs, private key blocks, JSON Web Tokens, GitHub and Slack tokens, Google API keys, Basic/Bearer header values, and URLs with an embedded user name and password
Values that cannot be credentials are ignored: shorter than 4 characters, containing whitespace, placeholders (changeme, <secret>, ****, ${...}), field names (u_password) and dotted names. Values built at run time are not checked. The finding never includes the value, only its line and length.
scan_linter_check.name: SEC-001: Hardcoded credential
scan_linter_check.resolution_details: Remove the credential from the script and rotate it, since it is exposed in update sets, version history and exports. Store it in a Credential record used through a Connection & Credential alias or a REST Message authentication profile, or in an encrypted (password2) system property read at run time.
scan_linter_check.short_description: A password, token, API key or other credential hardcoded in a string.
